title: Greatness in the Moment
hook: The discharge papers in a plastic tray turns greatness from a promise into work due before Friday.
counterintuition: Greatness can sound grand, yet it is built or lost in the small action currently waiting for your choice.
tryThisNow: Before your next important action, say what greatness would look like in that exact 10-minute window.
keyTakeaway: Shrink greatness from a distant identity into the quality of the action you choose in the current moment. The standard is visible action, not a better-sounding intention.

The tray, the chart, and the call are where the future gets built, one plain choice at a time.

examples.title: Charlotte slows the discharge

planSpec.audience: a practitioner in emergency department discharge workflow who needs the chapter move under real pressure
planSpec.stakes: the visible result will slip while everyone can still explain the effort
planSpec.requiredBeat: Charlotte uses the next discharge conversation as the standard of greatness.

examples.scenario: Discharge papers slide across the emergency department desk while Charlotte prepares for one more hurried patient conversation. She has said all week that patient experience matters. Now the patient is in front of her, confused and tired, and Charlotte must decide whether greatness is the speech she gives later or the clarity she offers in this minute. Charlotte signs the discharge note, checks the transport time, and asks the nurse beside her to confirm the patient is not waiting on paperwork.
examples.whatToDo: Make the next patient explanation the standard. Slow down, check understanding, and let the current conversation carry the value you claim.
examples.whyItMatters: The moment is the test. A future speech about care cannot repair a rushed explanation happening right now.

examples.title: Ben takes one more live call

planSpec.audience: a decision-maker in public radio pledge drive choosing whether to protect execution or drift
planSpec.stakes: the next 12 weeks will inherit a soft plan unless the decision is made now
planSpec.requiredBeat: Ben makes one pledge call with full attention instead of waiting for energy.

examples.scenario: "One more call before dinner?" Ben asks at the public radio pledge table, with phones lined along the wall. The room is flat after three hours. The station goal matters, but Ben has to choose the next live call, not the inspiring number on the poster. Ben chooses the clean repair step in the service bay and writes the inspection note before the next car rolls in.
examples.whatToDo: Take the next live call with full attention. Do not wait for energy to return before performing the commitment in front of you.
examples.whyItMatters: Commitment becomes performance on the next call. Ben turns a distant goal into the quality of one live action.

examples.title: Margaux writes the handoff now

planSpec.audience: a team lead in software incident response who needs visible proof before the week softens
planSpec.stakes: the team will mistake motion for progress if the proof stays hidden
planSpec.requiredBeat: Margaux handles the live incident note cleanly before talking about excellence.

examples.scenario: At 2:35 p.m. on the ward, Margaux reaches for discharge papers in a plastic tray. As charge nurse, she must decide whether to talk about patient flow or sign the next safe discharge step now. Margaux finishes the ward handoff sentence now, while the tray is still in front of her and the next patient is waiting.
examples.whatToDo: Write the handoff sentence now, not in the later debrief. Greatness shows in the live transfer of responsibility.
examples.whyItMatters: The outage handoff matters because someone else acts on it immediately. The later debrief is secondary to present execution.

examples.title: Lars reads the current file

planSpec.audience: a reflective operator in college admissions file review reading last week's failure as evidence
planSpec.stakes: a repeat failure will be explained away instead of corrected
planSpec.requiredBeat: Lars reviews one admissions file with the standard she claims to hold.

examples.scenario: It took Lars half a semester to notice that admissions excellence was not a committee value unless it touched the file in his hand. File boxes sit under the desk. He opens one borderline application and gives it the full attention he keeps promising in meetings. Lars updates the safety checklist at the loading dock instead of saving the fix for a later process meeting.
examples.whatToDo: Give the current file the committee standard. The value only counts when it changes the application being read now.
examples.whyItMatters: Lars makes the value real by applying it to the file, not by admiring it as an admissions principle.

examples.title: Sofia resets the saw

planSpec.audience: a reader in furniture workshop order queue comparing intention before the move with proof after it
planSpec.stakes: the work will stay aspirational unless the action changes in the room
planSpec.requiredBeat: Sofia cuts the joinery line correctly after the rush order arrives.

examples.scenario: At 7:50 a.m. in the service bay, Sofia checks torque specs beside a lift. As shop lead, she must decide whether quality is a slogan or whether this repair gets the careful inspection in front of her. Sofia runs the torque check in the service bay and has the apprentice read the spec back before the lift comes down.
examples.whatToDo: Reset the saw and make the cut correctly. Craftsmanship is measured at the line on the board, not in the language around it.
examples.whyItMatters: The corrected cut gives the standard a body. Without that action, craftsmanship stays a self-image.

examples.title: Akira checks the sample

planSpec.audience: two colleagues in Dublin design consultancy forcing the commitment into plain speech
planSpec.stakes: a public promise will dissolve unless someone names the proof and owner
planSpec.requiredBeat: Akira turns the client critique into one exact design decision.

examples.scenario: Which version of the design standard fits the next ten minutes? Akira asks in the Dublin consultancy as fabric samples sit beside a client brief. A partner wants a fast answer. Akira must decide whether the work gets the claimed standard now or only in tomorrow's recap. Akira ships the small bug fix with the test note attached, so the product standard exists in the build rather than in a promise.
examples.whatToDo: Apply the design standard to the brief in front of you. Name the decision, check the sample, and refuse a rushed answer that weakens the work.
examples.whyItMatters: Akira protects quality at the exact point where speed asks for a discount. That is present-tense performance.
